text:
maria: Heads-up: we started seeing a small but consistent tail-latency bump on the 8-GPU TP+PP jobs this morning (prod-sim, service=redwood-infer). +3-6% p99 across a few models.

alex: saw that in the alert dashboard. Any sign which phase? allreduce / kernel launch / host sync? :eyes:

maria: I pulled a short nvprof and our custom microtimers. The summary shows increased time at the TP boundary and an odd spike in ‘kv_prefetch_wait’ between steps. Snippet:```
microtimers: step_ms: 48.3
  compute_ms: 28.4
  allreduce_wait_ms: 8.6
  kv_prefetch_wait_ms: 6.7
  kernel_enqueue_ms: 4.6
```

chris: kv_prefetch_wait jumping sounds like the KV cache path is contending with the batching thread. Are we still using the new batching heuristic that merges small prefetched prefixes into the main batch?

maria: yes, the heuristic was flipped on for those clusters last week. Hypothesis: merging increases serialized memcpy/host-sync at TP boundaries and slows down the upstream perf-critical path.

alex: another angle: kernel selector logs show sometimes falling back to the 'generic_fp16' kernel when sequence length distribution is weird. That kernel has worse launch concurrency and may block the stream. We should log kernel choices per step and correlate with microtimers.

perf-bot: Automated capture queued -> nsight trace id: nsight-206872-9 (link: https://perf-team/nsight/nsight-206872-9). Captured 2 iterations with detailed kernel timelines.

chris: can someone run a minimal repro disabling the merge heuristic and disable KV prefetch? Quick command I used for local repro:```
python -m perf_tools.run --model rmt-3b --tp 2 --pp 4 --microtimer --disable-kv-prefetch --batch 1 --iters 20
```

sara: also add the env var DEBUG_KERNEL_SELECTOR=1 so we can annotate which kernel was chosen for each attention op. That will let us match kernel choices to allreduce stalls.

maria: ran that on a 8xA100 dev rig. Short results: disabling merge heuristic dropped kv_prefetch_wait_ms from 6.7 -> 1.9 and total step_ms from 48.3 -> 45.1. Still a 1.2ms extra in allreduce_wait on some steps.

alex: interesting — maybe merging changed ordering so larger allreduce payloads happen more frequently. Can you paste the custom timer breakdown when the allreduce spike occurs?

maria: pasted a short capture excerpt from the nsight timeline:```
# timeline slice (step 102)
[0.000] kernel: attn_fp16_opt (rank0, stream 3) duration 10.8ms
[0.011] allreduce start (ring) duration 3.1ms wait_for_stream_sync true
[0.014] kv_memcpy_h2d (stream 1) duration 2.9ms
[0.017] kernel: ffn_fp16_generic (stream 0) enqueue 1.2ms
```

chris: that line 'wait_for_stream_sync true' is the red flag. Allreduce is blocking a stream because of stream sync used to coordinate kv prefetch memcpy. We should avoid host-synchronous ops on the allreduce path.

sara: proposed fix: change prefetch memcpy to use CUDA events for async ordering instead of stream synchronization, and let the kernel selector prefer kernels that are stream-fence friendly.

alex: quick experiment idea: add a microtimer around rpc/allreduce that measures time spent blocked on stream wait vs time executing collective. That would separate scheduler stall vs network latency. Something like:```
start = now_ns()
stream.synchronize()  # before collective, current behavior
sync_ns = now_ns()
run_allreduce()
end_ns = now_ns()
blocked_ms = (sync_ns - start)/1e6
collective_ms = (end_ns - sync_ns)/1e6
```
But replace synchronize() with cudaEventElapsed to avoid forcing host block in production.

perf-bot: quick nvprof diff shows allreduce idle time increases by ~2.5ms when merge heuristic enabled (compare traces: nsight-206872-8 vs nsight-206872-9).

maria: agreed next steps: 1) instrument kernel selector to emit per-op kernel id (DEBUG_KERNEL_SELECTOR=1) and ship a small sample to perf logs; 2) flip KV prefetch to event-based ordering on staging and measure; 3) run batch-size sweep to see effect on merging heuristic; 4) small patch to avoid stream.synchronize() around allreduce (feature branch: reduce/blockless-collective).

chris: can I own (1) and (2)? I'll send a PR with event-based memcpy shim and selector logging.

maria: awesome. I'll coordinate the perf traces and add a dashboard that correlates 'kv_prefetch_wait_ms' with 'allreduce_blocked_ms' per step.

sara: ping me if you want test rigs. I'll schedule a 1-hour window for controlled captures. :thumbsup:

alex: thanks team — this looks actionable. If the event-based prefetch removes the blocking we can enable the merge heuristic back with confidence.

maria: closing loop: we aim to have candidate PRs and a controlled capture tomorrow EOD.
